stem: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Ana eats 3 slices. What fraction of the pizza did Ana eat?
hints: A fraction shows part of a whole. Count how many equal slices make the whole pizza.
The whole pizza has 8 equal slices, so 8 is the bottom number.
Put the number of slices Ana ate on top and the number of slices in the whole pizza on the bottom.

steps.action: Count the equal parts in the whole pizza: 8 slices.
steps.why: The bottom number of a fraction tells how many equal parts make one whole.

steps.action: Count the parts Ana ate: 3 slices.
steps.why: The top number tells how many of those parts you are talking about.

steps.action: Write the part over the whole: 3/8.
steps.why: Read 3/8 as "3 out of 8" or "three-eighths". The part goes on top and the whole goes on the bottom.
Ana did not eat the whole pizza, so the answer must be less than 8/8.

trapNotes.5/8: This is the part Ana did not eat (8 − 3 = 5 slices). The question asks what she ate.
trapNotes.8/3: This is upside down. The whole (8 slices) goes on the bottom, and the part (3 slices) goes on top.
trapNotes.3/5: This compares the 3 slices eaten with the 5 slices left. A fraction of the pizza needs all 8 slices on the bottom.
